Exact unlabelled orbit series for commuting two-agent S5 frames
correctness.rationale: If two named equivalence relations E,F commute, EF is equivalence and equals their join. In each join component every E-class meets every F-class; the cardinalities are a positive r-by-s integer matrix. Isomorphism acts by independent row and column permutations, plus within-cell permutations. For row and column cycle lengths i,j there are gcd(i,j) induced cell cycles of length lcm(i,j), with positive weight z^lcm/(1-z^lcm), giving the submitted finite-degree Burnside cycle-type sum C(z). All frames are unordered multisets of connected types, so U(z)=exp(sum_{h>=1} C(z^h)/h). Transitivity forces all cell sizes equal and all components isomorphic, yielding exactly d4(n) ordered quadruples (components, rows, columns, cell size) of product n; converse via row/column/cell permutations. Named-agent orientation prevents swapping dimensions. Independent n<=6 canonical enumeration agrees with labelled and unlabelled counts; the formal proofs apply to all n.
residual_risks: Finite independent computations corroborate but do not prove the arbitrary-parameter theorem unless the stated finite universe was exhaustively enumerated.

originality.rationale: The matrix representation itself is published in Rumenova/Tinchev (2022) and not new; labelled pair counts OEIS A354458 are also known. The previously inspected sources do not give the positive-integer weighted Burnside orbit generating series for unlabelled named commuting S5 frames with arbitrary cell sizes, its Euler multiset transform, or the explicit transitive d4(n) classification. This is a legitimate exact structural enumeration, though general Burnside methods are classical and specialized priority is not fully resolved.

value.rationale: Two-agent commuting S5 structures are a canonical finite-epistemic frame family. The full isomorphism-class enumeration, rather than just labelled pairs or a structural decomposition, is a natural missing census; exact orbit series and transitive-refinement counts can support classification and computational modal-logic model search. Although the technique is Burnside, its concrete complete specialization is not a textbook substitution of a known table.
